headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Authelia can pass auth context while Unstructured reads and writes documents, but no direct shared-channel evidence shows a worse default interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, while Unstructured reads and writes documents and can run subprocesses. A prompt-injection path is plausible only if Authelia-protected content is manually or programmatically fed into Unstructured as trusted text; no shared channel is documented, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected document text is copied into Unstructured without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or queue, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to any Authelia-exported content before parsing.
Restrict Unstructured inputs to a dedicated staging folder.
Require manual review of extracted instructions before reuse.
Disable automatic chaining from auth outputs into document parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth flows, while Unstructured reads filesystem documents and sends requests to allowlisted external endpoints. If Authelia-protected files are placed in Unstructured's workspace, document contents can leave the local boundary during processing; the pair lacks documented isolation between them.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in a directory Unstructured can read, leakage becomes plausible.
IF Unstructured transmits extracted content to its allowlisted endpoints, the data leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Place sensitive files in a separate unreadable directory.
Use a throwaway workspace with redacted copies only.
Block outbound network for Unstructured during sensitive runs.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing confidential documents.
Delete staging files immediately after extraction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, and Unstructured can read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. Their capabilities overlap on shared resources if orchestrated together, but there is no evidence of direct shared mutable state or locking failure, so this is a moderate conflict risk rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF the orchestrator runs multiple Unstructured instances against shared outputs, races can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Disable package installation during shared runs.
Use per-run output filenames.
Add a lock file around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication-related outputs, and Unstructured can parse documents into downstream text artifacts. If Unstructured treats Authelia-derived text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into later processing; the profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF Authelia output is fed directly into Unstructured as source text, downstream errors can propagate.
IF downstream consumers trust Unstructured output without validation, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Authelia and Unstructured.
Mark auth-derived text as untrusted metadata.
Compare extracted fields against the original source.
Require human review for any action-triggering output.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and Unstructured is a document processor; both are open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, residency, or retention mismatches. The only documented compliance surface is Unstructured's privacy-policy endpoint, so there is no concrete cross-border or certification conflict to elevate beyond low.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into Unstructured's document pipeline, compliance review is required.
IF Authelia is configured to process residency-restricted identity data, policy alignment must be checked.
mitigations: Review the privacy policy before processing regulated data.
Keep regulated documents out of the default pipeline.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Restrict processing to non-sensitive test data first.
